description: PASS: binary content carried as a base64-encoded string field. The digest is computed over the JSON representation — that is, over the base64 string as a JSON string, not over the decoded binary bytes. This is the correct encoding: jcs-n operates on the JSON payload as-is, so a 'content' field whose value is a base64 string is digested as a base64 string. A verifier that decodes the base64 before computing the digest would produce a different pre-image and a different digest; that verifier is non-conforming. The 'encoding' field is part of the payload and is included in the pre-image.
note: The 17 source bytes (PNG magic + IHDR start) encode to 'iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUg=='. The pre-image and digest are computed over that string. An implementation that strips the base64 encoding before hashing would produce a 32-byte SHA-256 over the decoded bytes instead — a completely different value with no indication of the mismatch.
